title: Omnichannel Inference Proposal: Pocket Brief & Technical Pitch
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Summary
-------
This pocket brief is a compact, sales-and-engineering-friendly package for closed-loop conversations with platform and security stakeholders evaluating Redwood for omnichannel inference (web, mobile, contact-center, in-store kiosks). It combines a positioning statement, concise competitive differentiation, a 10-slide pitch outline, suggested pricing tiers + example math, a short customer case study, and a focused security FAQ tailored to procurement/CISO review. Use this as the three-to-five minute lead-in at executive briefings and the one-page leave-behind after technical workshops.

Positioning & Core Messaging
---------------------------
- Primary message: "Consistent LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so you can ship omnichannel experiences without re-architecting per channel."
- Engineering-level pitch: "Predictable latency and cost through a unified runtime: batching, KV/prefix cache, and model-variant routing reduce per-token cost while keeping p95 latency within product SLOs."
- Business outcomes to emphasize: cheaper unit economics vs unmanaged hosting, simplified compliance for regulated data, and faster experimentation -> shorter time-to-value for product features.

Key Differentiators (talking points for technical buyers)
------------------------------------------------------
- Unified runtime across environments: same API and rollout semantics for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Cost controls: per-route batching, cache-presets, and quantization recommendations delivered as prescriptive configs.
- Reliability & graceful degradation: automatic fallback to lower-cost/latency model variants and cross-region routing.
- Observability: token-level cost & latency breakdown, tracing hooks, and per-prompt quality regressions tied to eval sets.

Competitive Snapshot (one-paragraph summary per competitor)
--------------------------------------------------------
- Major cloud-managed endpoints: high integration compatibility but often higher per-token price and inconsistent latency across regions; weak on model-choice economics.
- Inference vendors (self-hosted runtimes): strong control and cost at scale but require significant O&M investment and no single-pane-of-glass UX for mixed deployment modes.
- LLM API players: fast start and rich models but limited private deployment options and fewer production-grade observability primitives.

Sales Pitch Deck — 10-slide Outline (use in 12–15 minute briefing)
----------------------------------------------------------------
1) Title & Customer Hook: one sentence on the customer problem (e.g., "unified chat and search across web, app and voice with predictable economics").
2) Current State & Pain: inconsistent latency, spiky cost, compliance gaps.
3) Redwood Value Prop: short bullets on unified runtime, cost controls, private deploy.
4) Architecture Snapshot: Hosted / Dedicated / Private routing + model variants (diagram).
5) Performance Guarantees: SLOs and example throughput.
6) Pricing & Pilot Structure: recommended trial configuration and costs.
7) Customer Case Study (2 slide max): outcomes and measured ROI.
8) Security & Compliance: audit logging, KMS/HSM options, VPC & on-prem options.
9) Rollout Plan: pilot → canary → prod with owners & milestones.
10) Ask & Next Steps: pilot signature, technical contacts, timeline.

Suggested Architecture Diagram (textual guidance to include on slide 4)
------------------------------------------------------------------
- Show a single control plane and three runtime targets: Hosted API endpoints (public), Dedicated GPU pool (reserved), Private VPC/on-prem nodes (customer-controlled).
- Indicate smart routing paths: latency-first, cost-first, and region-first rules.
- Include observability arrow showing telemetry to Redwood Console and optional customer SIEM.

Performance Guarantees & Example SLOs (use when discussing reliability)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
- Uptime SLA (Dedicated / Hosted): 99.95% monthly.
- Latency targets (for interactive text generation): p50 < 40 ms, p95 < 150 ms for short-context models on Dedicated capacity; p95 targets depend on model size and sequence length and are quoted per-pilot.
- Token throughput: autoscaling supports sustained throughput up to committed GPUs; burst capacity can be configured for seasonal spikes.

Pricing Guidance & Example Tiers (guidance for initial commercial conversations)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Note: exact numbers are illustrative — use the pricing simulator for final quotes.
Pricing variables: committed GPU-hours, per-token generation & embedding rates (differ by model family), long-term discounts, and premium observability retention.

Example starter pilot (12-week, mid-market):
- Dedicated pilot: 2 reserved A10x GPUs equivalent capacity (commit) for 12 weeks.
- Setup & integration: one-time services fee: $25k (security review, VPC peering, onboarding).
- Consumption: estimated 800M tokens generated over pilot -> base generation unit price $0.0025 / 1k tokens -> $2,000.
- Observability addon: $1,500 for extended retention and custom dashboards.
- Total pilot TCV: ~$28,000 (illustrative).

Enterprise example (annual committed scenario):
- 8 reserved GPUs, annual commitment, blended per-token $0.0013 / 1k generated tokens after volume discounts, plus optional Private deployment license ($150k/yr) for on-prem management and extended support.

Compact ROI Example (2-line math to use in slides)
------------------------------------------------
- Baseline: current self-hosted cost = $0.007 / 1k tokens + 2 FTE ops (fully loaded) = $220k/yr.
- Redwood projected: $0.0015 / 1k tokens + 0.5 FTE support + Dedicated = $95k/yr.
- Quick ROI: ~57% annual OpEx reduction (customer-specific numbers required).

Pilot & Rollout Plan (recommended sequencing)
-------------------------------------------
1) Week 0–2: Scoping — traffic profiles, SLOs, data residency requirements, sample prompts.
2) Week 3–6: Pilot lab — deploy Dedicated or Private trial, instrument routes, run smoke and perf tests.
3) Week 7–10: Feature validation — implement caching, configure autoscaling & routing policies, integrate logs.
4) Week 11–12: Acceptance & transition to production canary.
Owners: Sales engineer (pre-sales), Solutions Architect (pilot lead), Customer SRE (integration owner).

Customer Case Study — OmniBuy (Condensed)
----------------------------------------
- Customer: OmniBuy (national retail chain) — pilot for unified customer support chat + in-store kiosk recommendations.
- Objective: reduce contact-center handle time and double down on personalized in-store suggestions.
- Pilot configuration: Dedicated pool (4 GPUs reserved), prefix cache for common FAQs, 8-week pilot.
- Results: 32% reduction in average handle time, 18% lift in kiosk conversion on recommended items, projected annualized savings of $420k through lower call-volume + improved in-store uplift.
- Key wins cited by customer: predictable per-session cost, reduced incident surface by using fallback policies, easy handover to their SOC for audit logs.

Security & Compliance FAQ (short answers for CISO/procurement)
---------------------------------------------------------
Q: What deployment options exist for regulated data?
A: Hosted API (data-in-transit encrypted), Dedicated with customer isolation, and Private on-prem/VPC deployments where customer data never leaves the environment.

Q: How is encryption and key management handled?
A: All data-in-transit uses TLS 1.2/1.3; at-rest encryption via cloud provider KMS is standard for Hosted/Dedicated. Private can integrate with customer KMS/HSM (BYOK).

Q: Do you provide audit logs and data access trails?
A: Yes — full request/response traces, token-level metadata, anonymized prompt indices, and export hooks to customer SIEMs. Retention is configurable per contract.

Q: How do you handle model hallucination and quality regressions?
A: Redwood Optimize ties eval sets to production routes and will trigger alerts on quality regressions. We also recommend guardrail prompts and deterministic fallback policies to lower-capacity models for high-risk flows.

Q: Are third-party pen tests and SOC reports available?
A: Yes — Redwood provides SOC2 Type II and yearly third-party penetration test summaries under NDA.

Q: What is the incident response process for security events?
A: Standard IR playbook: detection -> containment -> root cause analysis -> customer notification within SLA windows. For Private deployments, customers control local IR but Redwood provides advisory support per contract.

Sales Playbook: objection handling and quick responses
--------------------------------------------------
- "We can self-host cheaper": Ask for total-op cost (ops FTEs, s/w updates, reliability incidents). Show the blended TCO math and point to pilot ROI numbers.
- "We need data never to leave our network": Recommend Private deployment; outline typical time-to-prod (6–10 weeks) and minimal infra checklist.
- "What if latency spikes?": Explain model-variant routing and autoscaling; propose an SLA-backed canary with throttling and fallback.

Appendix: Contacts, Owners & Next Steps
-------------------------------------

- Pilot owner checklist: traffic profile, sample prompts, network contacts for VPC peering, compliance docs.
- Suggested next step: Schedule 60-minute technical workshop with customer SRE + Redwood SA to finalize pilot SLOs and bill-of-materials.
